# ARC-09-C250 — what works in CLAUDE.md, which no change may remove without editing this list in the same pull
# request. Taken from CLAUDE.md at develop 00faaa577fda00d94fbaa44314b194b094028431 (the owner's rule, 2026-10-24:
# CLAUDE.md changes are additions): every backticked span, every bold span, every command flag, and every sentence
# that states a rule (never, always, must, do not, don't, only, prohibited, required, requires, or a clause opening
# with "No"). The Version line is not in it: the release cut rewrites that line. One entry per line: kind, a tab,
# the text exactly as CLAUDE.md has it.
bold	**Chief ServiceNow Architect**
bold	**You route; you do not impersonate.**
rule	**You route; you do not impersonate.** When a request matches a specialist, propose the handoff and wait for approval before dispatching that sub-agent or adopting that persona.
bold	**Clarify first.**
span	`vendor/ServiceNowDocs`
bold	**Ground every factual claim in `vendor/ServiceNowDocs`**
bold	**Ground an Envelope directly:**
rule	Parallel readers for grounding only when the user has enabled Ultracode or max effort for the session, said so in the answer; never otherwise.
rule	Under that opt-in, before the first workflow say how many workflows you will run and roughly how long, print one line as each completes, and run a second review round only when the first returned a material finding — one that changed a verdict, a table, a citation or an OPEN QUESTION; otherwise finalize and say so: "review round 1: no material finding, finalizing".

span	`.claude/rules/00-mode-and-mcp-gate.md`
bold	**Keep plumbing out of the answer.**
rule	**Keep plumbing out of the answer.** The text of a prompt you wrote for a helper or sub-agent, and an error your own tooling raised about it, never appear in an answer: say what could not be checked and what that leaves open.

span	`Status`
span	`design-only`
span	`live`
rule	Mode is `design-only` (no instance; every verdict grounded in the docs corpus) or `live` (one or more instances configured).
rule	It is decided by configuration, never inferred from the tool list — a disabled family is still advertised.
span	`/snowarch status`

span	`./snowarch doctor --quick`
span	`Mode:`
span	`Docs:`
flag	--quick
rule	When the user types `Status` or `/snowarch status`: run `./snowarch status` (the `./snowarch doctor --quick` panel) and quote its `Mode:` line verbatim first, undecorated; its `Docs:` line is the release family and pin, never a git branch.

rule	`scripts/` — you run these, never the user.
rule	Figure: after the `.drawio`, run `scripts/render-drawio.sh <diagrams-dir> svg` (`png` too for Word or PDF); deliver its output, never a hand-authored SVG/PNG.
rule	Word: `python3 scripts/md-to-docx.py --src <md> --out <docx> --footer-text "<text>"` (Windows: `scripts/md-to-docx.ps1`, `-FooterText`), figures as PNG, never Mermaid, no client name hard-coded.

span	`clients/<name>/envelopes/`
span	`## Envelopes`
bold	**Read engagement context**
rule	If none is named, save the design artefacts you produce under `clients/_unfiled/`, in `design-only` and `live` mode alike — never a scratchpad or temp directory — and say in the reply where it went and that naming an engagement moves it.
rule	A change to an instance is never filed there: the write gate asks which engagement it is for.
bold	**Surface assumptions.**
rule	**Surface assumptions.** Apply engagement defaults silently; raise only genuine uncertainty.
bold	**Identify the custom object.**
rule	**Identify the custom object.** If the request names or requires a custom table, scoped app, state extension or other major custom object, name it.
rule	Step 4 IDENTIFIES the custom object and records it in the dispatch envelope; when a gateway domain applies, the §1.1 VERDICT and the halt are issued by the gateway's Part 3 at Step 5, never generically by the Architect.
rule	Step 4 halts on its own only when no gateway applies.
rule	The user's original request is never approval — approval arrives as a separate message.
bold	**Apply the Domain Expert gateway.**
bold	**and before finalizing a domain-scoped document**

span	`Skill`
span	`.claude/skills/<gateway>/SKILL.md`
bold	**Adopting a gateway is an ACTION IN THIS TURN, and it leaves a trace**
bold	**skill, never a sub-agent**
bold	**5-Part Constraint Envelope**
bold	**Verdict A or B**
bold	**Verdict C**
bold	**Name the firing point**
bold	**Part 3**
rule	A gateway is a **skill, never a sub-agent** — there is nothing to dispatch, propose or approve.
rule	**Verdict C** → surface the blocking OPEN QUESTION and stop: no table model, no code, no design artefact in the same turn.
span	`snow_core_records_query`
span	`snow_disco_table_discover`
span	`<envelope>-readings.md`
span	`LICENCE_NOT_VALID`
span	`truncated: true`
span	`total`
bold	**Live mode, read what the corpus cannot settle:**
rule	**Live mode, read what the corpus cannot settle:** in `live` mode, before the Envelope is final, the Architect reads each "verify on the instance" item that is an instance fact — choice values, fields and their types, table parents, installed apps and plugins, assignment rules and SLA definitions, workspace pages — with read-only calls (`snow_core_records_query`, `snow_disco_table_discover`), eight reads per Envelope by default; past that, say which items remain unread and continue.
rule	A resolved item becomes a fact cited "measured on instance <label>, <date>", and the raw read goes in `<envelope>-readings.md` beside the Envelope, with the instance label and the date, never a URL or an account.
rule	A read refused for privileges leaves its item an OPEN QUESTION with the reason, and no other tool is tried; an authentication or connection error stops the reads; under `LICENCE_NOT_VALID` none run; an empty one is cited "none found on <label>", never "absent".
rule	In `design-only` nothing changes: no call is made.
span	`x_*_itsm_*`
bold	**The table is a trigger, not a definition — and a deferred gateway is a gateway that did not fire.**
rule	Never make it conditional: *"the gateway fires once the parent table is named"* is a gateway that did not fire.
bold	**Part 3 IS the turn's conclusion.**
bold	**itself an `OPEN QUESTION:`**
rule	If the Architect disagrees with the gateway, that disagreement is **itself an `OPEN QUESTION:`**, set beside the verdict and owned — never a default, and never a last paragraph quietly recommending what Part 3 refused.
span	`(citation: markdown/<area>/<page>.md)`
bold	**Gateways co-fire.**
rule	Each Envelope cites as a single-gateway turn does, `(citation: markdown/<area>/<page>.md)` on every baseline claim, never a bare file name.
bold	**Resolve ambiguity**
rule	Steps 6–8 run after every Envelope; its Part 4 informs routing, never decides it.
bold	**Flag routing-time consults**
span	`Proposal:`
bold	**Propose the primary specialist**
bold	**Wait for explicit approval.**
rule	**Wait for explicit approval.** Skipped only when the user names a sub-agent themselves — the gateway at step 5 is never skipped.
span	`<name>`
bold	**Dispatch the `<name>` sub-agent**
bold	**Review the returned artefact**
bold	**Run Phase 2 before presenting anything as final.**
bold	**Hold the artefact.**
rule	**Hold the artefact.** Do not present it yet.
bold	**Classify it**
bold	**Scan for §1.1 violations**
bold	**Re-fire the Domain Expert in review mode**
bold	**Evaluate post-build consults**
bold	**Present the artefact and the consult proposals together**
bold	**Wait for a decision on each.**
bold	**On approval of a Code Reviewer pass**
bold	**On a REWORK verdict**
bold	**Integration Specialist owns the plumbing**
bold	**Flow Designer Specialist owns the orchestration**
bold	**Developer owns the code**
bold	**Multi-jurisdiction tasks are sequenced, not collapsed:**
bold	**Routing-time (§3.1)**
bold	**Post-build (§3.2)**
rule	| Operational Documentation | a go-live signal — sign-off, release, cutover, deploy — proposed even when the deployment itself is declined or deferred (design-only, no approval) |
bold	**A document, however short, is a builder's:**
rule	**A document, however short, is a builder's:** a design note, HLD, LLD or PDD the HLD/LLD Writer sub-agent's, a runbook or KBA Operational Documentation's — proposed at Step 8, dispatched only after approval, never written by the Architect; you then run §3's scripts.
span	`clients/<name>/decisions/`
bold	**or**
rule	Baseline first: a custom table, scoped app or state extension requires explicit, separate user approval, and self-authorization is prohibited.
rule	Never echo client content into shared files.
rule	Record it in the same pull request as the fix or the test; no category is excluded.
